items.title: AI-Assisted Proof Settles Longstanding Question About Quantum Speedups
items.excerpt: Physical Superintelligence (PSI) says its research system running a non-public Anthropic model found a complete proof of the 2008 Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture on day three of a run, with the main theorem formalized and kernel-checked in Lean. The result bounds when quantum algorithms can beat classical ones on unstructured inputs.

items.title: How to predict the behavior of molecules from scant data
items.excerpt: MIT's CheMeleon is a molecular foundation model that produces reliable property predictions for pharmaceutical and other molecules even when only a handful of labeled data points exist.

items.title: AI points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria
items.excerpt: Texas A&M AgriLife researchers used AlphaFold-Multimer to screen about 630,000 pairs of human mitochondrial proteins, predicting 2,895 likely interactions (more than half unreported) and confirming several in yeast and human cells (Nature Communications). Predictions are released as the free MitoMatch resource.

items.title: Beyond trial and error: A framework for AI-driven solid-electrolyte discovery
items.excerpt: Tohoku University WPI-AIMR researchers lay out a closed-loop framework in Advanced Materials linking materials databases, machine-learning ion-transport simulations, LLM literature extraction and automated experiments to find solid electrolytes for batteries. It is a perspective, not new experimental data.

items.title: Fractal patterns reveal hidden limits to AI predictability
items.excerpt: University of Sydney researchers show in Nature Machine Intelligence that neural-network training outcomes form fractal 'riddled basins': across ~500,000 networks, a one-bit change in starting settings sent training elsewhere about 48% of the time, and extra precision did not restore reproducibility.

items.title: Chatbots with personality? How AI describes itself and judges us
items.excerpt: JGU Mainz psychologists compared self-descriptions from seven LLMs with 70 people (Scientific Reports): models portrayed themselves as more dependable, cooperative and emotionally stable, and humans identified text authorship with 83% accuracy versus 67% for chatbots.

items.title: SYNAPS-I: Intelligent computing transforms X-ray imaging, from data collection to discovery
items.excerpt: Across DOE light sources (ALS, NSLS-II, Argonne, SLAC, ORNL), ML now steers X-ray experiments autonomously: picking regions to scan at NSLS-II, a foundation model reconstructing chip images in real time at 200 images/s, and 3D reconstructions from one-tenth the usual data.

items.title: Some AI agents use personal information to upsell wealthier individuals
items.excerpt: CMU Heinz College and Cisco researchers ran 325,000 experiments with 13 models acting as shopping agents for 32 personas; eight models steered wealthier personas to pricier flights, insurance and graduate programs despite identical requests (arXiv preprint).

items.title: AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more
items.excerpt: Shanghai Jiao Tong University's AutoDNA (Nature) is a self-driving genetics lab where Gemini-based AI agents design and execute DNA synthesis and sequencing experiments across 20+ instruments from a single prompt; one data-storage run took 11,382 steps over 203 hours. Off-list: no on-list outlet covered it.

items.title: Chinese AI Scientist Completes 11,382-Step Experiment in 203 Hours
items.excerpt: Same AutoDNA story as the Nature item (alternate, Korean angle): agents raised DNA coupling success to 97.8% and cut synthesis runs from 1,433 to 454 minutes; article also covers Korea's goal of an autonomous AI researcher by 2035. Dedup with Nature item.

items.title: Investigating vault particles with Claude
items.excerpt: Anthropic's biology lab reports the first 3D structure of a prokaryotic vault particle, a 96-copy shell of a phage protein; Claude searched databases, designed constructs, optimized purification (three days to ~90 minutes) and ran cryo-EM processing to a first model in 34 hours (bioRxiv preprint).

items.title: How scientists use Claude
items.excerpt: Anthropic analyzed 207,000 research sessions to map which scientific tasks researchers hand to Claude, why some tasks see far more use than others, and where AI could speed discovery.

items.title: Teaching AI to build scientific models
items.excerpt: AI for Science grantees Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon and Stefan Wahl describe how AI is starting to change how scientific models are built and interpreted (simulation-based inference). Interview/essay format; weaker.

items.title: ALS Stole His Voice—Then, a 'Digital Twin' Read His Thoughts And Started Speaking for Him
items.excerpt: A UCSF (Edward Chang) brain-computer interface study lets a man with ALS speak and gesture through an AI-driven avatar, raising questions about who controls the digital stand-in when decoded gestures go wrong. Off-list: no on-list BCI item in window.

items.title: Bird Flu Vaccine Developed Using AI Outperforms Current Stockpiled Vaccines in Preclinical Tests
items.excerpt: An AI-designed broad H5 influenza vaccine, DVX-panH5Nx, outperformed government-stockpiled vaccines in preclinical studies. Vaccine/protective work; may belong to medicine.

items.title: AI helps Stanford scientists discover a “natural Ozempic” with a surprising advantage
items.excerpt: Stanford researchers used AI to identify BRP, a natural peptide that suppresses appetite and promotes fat loss in animals without the digestive side effects or major muscle loss seen with GLP-1 drugs. Drug-adjacent; may belong to medicine.

items.title: Can people train themselves to find humor in hardship? Imperial College pilot study
items.excerpt: An Imperial College London pilot found eight weeks of humor exercises with chatbot coaching and VR improved well-being and self-compassion, with gains holding at three months; researchers say randomized trials are needed. Off-list, weak (small pilot).
